sentences.zh: 不是因为他像个意大利人。

sentences.en: No, I don't think he's a voluble and doing excessive gesturing or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 对，我觉得他并不健谈，也没有什么过度的手势之类的。

sentences.en: I think quite the opposite, actually.
sentences.zh: 我觉得恰恰相反，实际上。

sentences.en: I think he's very reserved.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他非常内向。

sentences.en: And Löwenhaupt is the kind of man who will follow his orders to the absolute letter, you know, in the face of the most overwhelming danger.
sentences.zh: 而勒旺豪普特正是那种会绝对不折不扣执行命令的人，你知道的，哪怕面对最压倒性的危险。

sentences.en: But he's not great at thinking for himself and using his own initiative.
sentences.zh: 但他不太擅长独立思考和发挥自主性。

sentences.en: Now, he had set off from Riga late.
sentences.zh: 当时，他很晚才从里加出发。

sentences.en: It had taken him ages to get these 2,000 wagons of supplies together.
sentences.zh: 他花了极长的时间才把这2000辆补给大车凑齐。

sentences.en: He's got about 12,000 men and he's made very, very slow progress through Latvia and
sentences.zh: 他手下大约有12,000人，在穿过拉脱维亚和……时，进展非常非常缓慢。

sentences.en: Lithuania.
sentences.zh: 立陶宛。

sentences.en: Again, the problem is the weather.
sentences.zh: 同样，问题出在天气上。

sentences.en: It's pouring with rain.
sentences.zh: 下着倾盆大雨。

sentences.en: The terrain is so wet and muddy that these wagons are always getting stuck and his men are having to effectively build
sentences.zh: 地形又湿又泥泞，以至于这些大车总是陷进去，他的手下不得不实际上建造……

sentences.en: kind of makeshift roads of timber for the wagons to roll over them as they go through these kind of marshes and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 一种由木头搭成的简易路面，好让大车在穿过这类沼泽之类的地方时从上面碾过去。

sentences.en: Charles waits and waits for Löwenhaupt in Mogilev.
sentences.zh: 查理在莫吉廖夫等待着勒旺豪普特。

sentences.en: He waits for a month.
sentences.zh: 他等了一个月。

sentences.en: Then he waits for another month.
sentences.zh: 接着他又等了一个月。

sentences.en: It's now in the middle of August and there was still no sign of this Baltic relief column.
sentences.zh: 现在已经是八月中旬，却依然没有这支波罗的海增援纵队的影踪。

sentences.en: His men are getting very restless and their horses have run out of fodder, out of food.
sentences.zh: 他的手下开始变得非常躁动，他们的马匹也已经草料耗尽、没有食物了。

sentences.en: So now he thinks, okay, I won't wait any longer.
sentences.zh: 所以现在他想，好吧，我不能再等了。

sentences.en: I'm just going to press on and this guy can catch up with me later.
sentences.zh: 我得继续前进了，这家伙以后可以再追上我。

sentences.en: So he crosses the Dnieper and by the 11th of September, he is just 50 miles outside Smolensk.
sentences.zh: 于是他渡过了第聂伯河，到9月11日时，他距离斯摩棱斯克仅有50英里。

sentences.en: But they really don't have any food at this point.
sentences.zh: 但此时他们实在没有任何食物。

sentences.en: And the mercenaries he has hired from Germany are very, very unhappy.
sentences.zh: 而他从德国雇来的雇佣兵非常非常不高兴。

sentences.en: You know, we've signed up for this.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们当初签了约。

sentences.en: We thought this was going to be a great campaign and we're just incredibly hungry.
sentences.zh: 我们以为这将是一场伟大的战役，而我们现在饿得难以置信。

sentences.en: Everywhere they look, there's a huge pool of black smoke over the fields.
sentences.zh: 无论他们望向哪里，田野上空都弥漫着一大片滚滚黑烟。

sentences.en: The fields are burning.
sentences.zh: 田野在燃烧。

sentences.en: So thick it was said that it blotted out the sun.
sentences.zh: 据说浓烟滚滚，甚至遮蔽了太阳。

sentences.en: And at night, in the darkness, they can see the red glow of the countryside burning all the way to Slametsk because, of course, Peter's men have set it alight.
sentences.zh: 到了夜里，在黑暗中，他们可以看到一路延伸到斯拉梅茨克的乡村燃烧的红光，因为彼得的手下当然已经把它点燃了。

sentences.en: So now Charles faces a fateful decision.
sentences.zh: 因此，查理现在面临着一个重大的决定。

sentences.en: He could go back to the river, to the Dnieper, to the rendezvous point and wait for Leuvenhaupt.
sentences.zh: 他可以回到河边，回到第聂伯河，回到会合点去等待勒旺豪普特。

sentences.en: Or change direction.
sentences.zh: 或者改变方向。

sentences.en: Instead of continuing towards Slametsk and then Moscow, he could turn south towards a Russian province called Severia, which is on the border of modern day Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 与其继续前往斯拉梅茨克然后进攻莫斯科，他可以调头向南，去一个叫做谢韦里亚的俄罗斯省份，那里位于现代乌克兰的边境。

sentences.en: Now, why would he do that?
sentences.zh: 那么，他为什么要这么做呢？

sentences.en: The answer, because the fields there haven't been burned.
sentences.zh: 答案是，因为那里的田野还没有被烧毁。

sentences.en: So they could rest in this area.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可以在这个地区休整。

sentences.en: They could get the food they need.
sentences.zh: 他们可以获得所需的食物。

sentences.en: And then perhaps they could turn back towards the road to Moscow.
sentences.zh: 然后也许他们可以折返回通往莫斯科的道路。

sentences.en: And Charles is a gambler.
sentences.zh: 而查理是个赌徒。

sentences.en: He hates going back.
sentences.zh: 他讨厌走回头路。

sentences.en: He hates retreating.
sentences.zh: 他讨厌撤退。

sentences.en: So it's pretty obvious which he's going to pick.
sentences.zh: 所以他会选择哪一个，这就相当明显了。

sentences.en: He's never going to go back to the river, to the rendezvous point.
sentences.zh: 他绝不会回到河边，回到那个会合点。

sentences.en: He's going to say to his men, yeah, why not?
sentences.zh: 他会对手下说，对啊，为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Why not head south towards
sentences.zh: 为什么不向南前往……

sentences.en: Ukraine?
sentences.zh: 乌克兰呢？

sentences.en: We can find food there.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在那里找到食物。

sentences.en: And we're kind of going slightly off piste and off track, but...
sentences.zh: 我们有点偏离既定路线和轨道了，但是……

sentences.en: And they're a long way from Sweden.
sentences.zh: 而且他们离瑞典非常遥远。

sentences.en: Oh yeah, we're going a lot further away from Sweden, but we're only kind of going the wrong way so that we can go the right way later.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，我们离瑞典更远了，但我们只是在朝错误的方向走，这样以后才能朝正确的方向走。

sentences.en: That's kind of his thinking.
sentences.zh: 这差不多就是他的想法。

sentences.en: So it is on the 15th of
sentences.zh: 所以就在9月……

sentences.en: September, he says to his men, we break camp.
sentences.zh: 15日，他对部下说，我们拔营。

sentences.en: We head south towards Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 我们向南朝乌克兰进发。

sentences.en: This will, by the way, will be the single most disastrous decision of his life.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这将是他一生中最灾难性的决定。

sentences.en: Because three days later,
sentences.zh: 因为三天后，……

sentences.en: Leuvenhaupt does reach the rendezvous point on the Znieper.
sentences.zh: 勒旺豪普特确实抵达了第聂伯河上的会合点。

sentences.en: And when he gets there, there's no sign of the king.
sentences.zh: 当他到达那里时，不见国王的踪影。

sentences.en: But there are messengers who say to him, the king has changed his plans.
sentences.zh: 但有信使对他说，国王已经改变了计划。

sentences.en: He wants you to press on south as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 他希望你尽快向南推进。

sentences.en: But of course, Leuvenhaupt and his guys are totally exhausted.
sentences.zh: 但当然，勒旺豪普特和他的手下已经精疲力竭。

sentences.en: They've been trudging through all this mud for months.
sentences.zh: 他们几个月来一直在烂泥中跋涉。

sentences.en: So they start very miserably to head across the river and to head south.
sentences.zh: 于是他们极其凄凉地开始渡过河流并向南进发。

sentences.en: And then to his horror, his scouts report, they can see Russian cavalry on the horizon.
sentences.zh: 接着，令他惊恐的是，侦察兵报告说，他们在地平线上看到了俄罗斯骑兵。

sentences.en: So the Russians are coming.
sentences.zh: 所以俄罗斯人来了。

sentences.en: And what's obviously happened is Peter, who up to this point has never been a great military tactician.
sentences.zh: 显而易见的情况是，在此之前从未算得上出色军事战术家的彼得，……

sentences.en: You know, he hasn't actually been one of the great commanders of history by any means.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他绝算不上历史上伟大的统帅之一。

sentences.en: But he has spotted this gap between the two Swedish armies.
sentences.zh: 但他发现了这两支瑞典军队之间的空隙。

sentences.en: And he said, let's let Charles go to Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 他说，让查理去乌克兰吧。

sentences.en: We'll deal with this Baltic relief column.
sentences.zh: 我们来对付这支波罗的海增援纵队。

sentences.en: Let's hoover this up.
sentences.zh: 把这支吃掉。

sentences.en: He's actually adopting Charles's tactics.
sentences.zh: 他其实在采用查理的战术。

sentences.en: Yeah, I guess so.
sentences.zh: 对，我想是的。

sentences.en: You know, target one of your enemies and leave the other and then...
sentences.zh: 你知道的，瞄准你的一个敌人，放过另一个，然后……

sentences.en: Yes, target the weaker one, deal with that.
sentences.zh: 是的，瞄准较弱的那一个，解决它。

sentences.en: And then we'll...
sentences.zh: 然后我们……

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So by the 28th of September, Leuvenhaupt has been cornered by Peter near a village called
sentences.zh: 所以在9月28日之前，勒旺豪普特在靠近一个叫……的村庄时被彼得逼入绝境，……

sentences.en: Lesnaya, with his back to the river.
sentences.zh: 列斯纳亚，背靠着河。

sentences.en: The numbers are roughly equal.
sentences.zh: 双方兵力大致相当。

sentences.en: The Swedes are exhausted, though, after this ridiculous march through all this mud.
sentences.zh: 不过，在经历了这荒谬的泥泞行军之后，瑞典人已经筋疲力尽了。

sentences.en: Peter orders the attack around midday.
sentences.zh: 彼得在正午左右下令进攻。

sentences.en: It lasts all afternoon.
sentences.zh: 战斗持续了整个下午。

sentences.en: It's a horribly kind of attritional, muddy, bloody, miserable encounter.
sentences.zh: 这是一场极其消耗、泥泞、血腥而凄惨的遭遇战。

sentences.en: The Swedes, of course, because they're so good, even though they're exhausted, they acquit themselves pretty well.
sentences.zh: 当然，由于瑞典人非常优秀，尽管精疲力竭，他们的表现还是相当不错的。

sentences.en: And so as night falls and the snow starts falling inevitably, the honours are roughly even.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着夜幕降临，雪花开始不可避免地飘落，双方战局大致相当。

sentences.en: And in fact, the snowstorm is so fierce they can't continue.
sentences.zh: 事实上，暴风雪如此猛烈，他们无法继续战斗。

sentences.en: The Russians fall back a bit.
sentences.zh: 俄军略微退后。

sentences.en: And now Leuvenhaupt has a choice to make.
sentences.zh: 现在勒旺豪普特得做出抉择了。

sentences.en: And he says to his men, look, we can't stay here.
sentences.zh: 他对部下说，听着，我们不能留在这里。

sentences.en: We're absolutely shattered.
sentences.zh: 我们彻底累垮了。

sentences.en: I can't face a second day of this.
sentences.zh: 我无法再面对这样的一天。

sentences.en: Our priority must be to head on south and catch up with the king.
sentences.zh: 我们的首要任务必须是继续向南，追赶国王。

sentences.en: And that means we can't take this supply train with us, the thing they've been escorting all this way.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们不能把这支补给纵队带在身边，就是他们一路护送的这个东西。

sentences.en: He says, we just have to destroy it.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们只能摧毁它。

sentences.en: We don't want it to fall into enemy hands.
sentences.zh: 我们可不想让它落入敌手。

sentences.en: These cannons that they have been dragging for hundreds of miles, they lift them out of the wagons and they bury them underground and then they set fire to the wagons.
sentences.zh: 他们拖行了数百英里的这些大炮，被从大车上卸下来埋在地下，然后他们放火烧了这些大车。

sentences.en: This doesn't seem a display of master strategy.
sentences.zh: 这看起来可不像是高超战略的展现。

sentences.en: Well, no, I suppose it isn't.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没错，我想确实不是。

sentences.en: What else could he do though?
sentences.zh: 不过他还能做什么呢？

sentences.en: The supply train is really slowing him down.
sentences.zh: 补给纵队真的把他的速度拖慢了。

sentences.en: I suppose he could stand and fight for a second day.
sentences.zh: 我想他可以坚守并再打一天。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But his men are so tired that he thinks, you know, we're really risking disaster then.
sentences.zh: 但他的人太累了，以至于他觉得，你知道的，那样我们真的会面临灾难的风险。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So maybe I'm being harsh on him.
sentences.zh: 所以也许我对他的要求太苛刻了。

sentences.en: You're not Tom because actually what then happens is a complete and utter catastrophe.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你可没苛刻，因为接下来发生的实际上是一场彻头彻尾的灾难。

sentences.en: And the Swedes behave in a very un-Scandinavian way, I would say.
sentences.zh: 而且瑞典人的表现一点也不像斯堪的纳维亚人，依我看。

sentences.en: So they've set their own wagons on fire and in the darkness, some of the soldiers decide they will loot the wagons of their officers and they get stuck into their brandy.
sentences.zh: 所以他们点燃了自己的大车，而在黑暗中，一些士兵决定洗劫他们军官的大车，还大肆享用了他们的白兰地。

sentences.en: They're all tanked up on brandy, which goes straight to their heads because they're so tired.
sentences.zh: 他们都灌满了白兰地，由于太累了，这酒直冲脑门。

sentences.en: Discipline completely falls apart.
sentences.zh: 纪律彻底崩溃了。

sentences.en: Some of the Swedes say, let's just run for it.
sentences.zh: 一些瑞典人说，我们逃跑吧。

sentences.en: And they run off into the foreSt. Some of them even to say, we're doomed.
sentences.zh: 于是他们逃进了森林。甚至有人说，我们死定了。

sentences.en: Let's desert to the Russians.
sentences.zh: 向俄罗斯人投降吧。

sentences.en: And the army begins to fragment.
sentences.zh: 军队开始四分五裂。

sentences.en: And in the darkness, Cossack horsemen kind of come out of the woods and set upon little kind of groups of the Swedish bloke staggering drunkenly around.
sentences.zh: 在黑暗中，哥萨克骑兵从树林里冲出来，向那些酩酊大醉、东倒西歪的瑞典小分队发起猛攻。

sentences.en: And by dawn, as dawn breaks, Lovenhaupt has just about managed to restore order among his troops.
sentences.zh: 到了黎明破晓时，勒旺豪普特总算勉强在军队中恢复了秩序。

sentences.en: But in the chaos of about 12,000 men, he has lost perhaps 6,000 overnight.
sentences.zh: 但在大约12,000人的混乱中，他在一夜之间可能损失了6,000人。

sentences.en: He've either wandered into the snow, they've drowned, they've been picked off by the Cossacks.
sentences.zh: 他们要么迷失在雪地里，要么溺水身亡，要么被哥萨克人逐个消灭。

sentences.en: Is this what inspires the Swedes to make alcohol so expensive?
sentences.zh: 这就是启发瑞典人把酒卖得这么贵的原动力吗？

sentences.en: Almost certainly.
sentences.zh: 几乎可以肯定。

sentences.en: They learnt their lesson.
sentences.zh: 他们吸取了教训。

sentences.en: Almost certainly.
sentences.zh: 几乎可以肯定。

sentences.en: I hadn't thought of that, but yeah, they have learnt their lesson.
sentences.zh: 我之前没想到这点，不过是的，他们确实吸取了教训。

sentences.en: So he's lost everything.
sentences.zh: 所以他失去了一切。

sentences.en: He's lost all the clothing, the uniforms, the gunpowder, the muskets, the medicines, the cannons on which Charles was counting.
sentences.zh: 他失去了所有的衣物、军服、火药、滑膛枪、药品以及查理指望的大炮。

sentences.en: A total and utter catastrophe.
sentences.zh: 一场彻头彻尾的灾难。

sentences.en: He manages to get the 6,000 men away and they stagger south towards Charles's camp in Sevilla where they arrive 10 days later.
sentences.zh: 他设法把剩下的6,000人带了出来，他们蹒跚着向南朝查理在谢韦里亚的营地撤退，并在10天后抵达。

sentences.en: And you can imagine Charles's face falling when he sees them.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象查理看到他们时脸都垮了下来。

sentences.en: Like, where are all the wagons?
sentences.zh: 就像在问，大车都到哪儿去了？

sentences.en: But can you?
sentences.zh: 但真的是这样吗？

sentences.en: I actually imagine his face not falling.
sentences.zh: 我其实想象的是他的脸并没有垮下来。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're probably right.
sentences.zh: 是的，你可能说得对。

sentences.en: He would preserve his mask of son foie.
sentences.zh: 他会保持他那镇定自若的面具。

sentences.en: But inside, there'd be a little, maybe a little twitch of his mouth.
sentences.zh: 但在内心深处，可能会有一丝，也许嘴角会微微抽搐。

sentences.en: Or maybe he would give a kind of cold half-smile as he realised.
sentences.zh: 或者当他意识到时，他可能会露出一丝冷酷的微笑。

sentences.en: Like Spain Fortbeard.
sentences.zh: 就像带胡子的西班牙人一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: A cold half-smile as he realised that God had set him a tougher challenge than ever.
sentences.zh: 当他意识到上帝给他出了一个前所未有的巨大挑战时，他露出了冷酷的半笑。

sentences.en: But he would never doubt that it was a challenge he was bound to pass.
sentences.zh: 但他绝不会怀疑这是一个他注定能通过的挑战。

sentences.en: He would sort of say, well, this will make the reports of my ultimate victory even more glowing.
sentences.zh: 他大概会说，嗯，这会让最终胜利的战报显得更加光彩夺目。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That we've done it without all these supplies.
sentences.zh: 我们在没有所有这些补给的情况下做到了这一点。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Peter is delighted.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，彼得欣喜若狂。

sentences.en: Effectively, he's knocked one of these two Swedish armies out.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他已经消灭了两支瑞典军队中的一支。

sentences.en: So Peter goes and holds a triumph.
sentences.zh: 所以彼得去举行了一场凯旋仪式。

sentences.en: He has a triumph in Smolensk.
sentences.zh: 他在斯摩棱斯克举行了凯旋式。

sentences.en: Well, it's the third Rome, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 好吧，这里可是第三罗马，不是吗？

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He forces Swedish prisoners to march through the streets with their flags.
sentences.zh: 他强迫瑞典战俘带着他们的旗帜游行过街。

sentences.en: He has, it's the first time really I think that he does this and it really imprints itself in the European imagination.
sentences.zh: 他的确这么做了，我认为这是他第一次这样做，而且这确实深深印入了欧洲人的想象之中。

sentences.en: He has battle descriptions and plans of the Battle of Lesnaya printed in Russian and in Dutch.
sentences.zh: 他把列斯纳亚战役的战斗描述和作战计划用俄语和荷兰语印发了出来。

sentences.en: Charles XII is marching southwards.

sentences.en: And he is marching towards a country that has, of course, been in the news a great deal recently.
sentences.zh: 他正朝着一个最近频频登上新闻的国家进发。

sentences.en: And that is Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 那个国家就是乌克兰。

sentences.en: And Dominic, if there's one thing that people know about the history of Ukraine, it's unbelievably complicated, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，如果说人们对乌克兰历史有什么了解的话，那就是它复杂得令人难以置信，对吧？

sentences.en: It is complicated.
sentences.zh: 确实很复杂。

sentences.en: So Ukrainian history in the 17th century 101.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们来上一堂17世纪乌克兰历史的入门课。

sentences.en: So most of modern Ukraine had been part of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth for centuries.
sentences.zh: 现代乌克兰的大部分地区几个世纪以来一直是波兰-立陶宛联邦的一部分。

sentences.en: And you can divide its population incredibly roughly and simplistically into four groups.
sentences.zh: 你可以极其粗略、简单地把这里的人口分成四类。

sentences.en: There's a Polish landowning elite in Ukraine, Polish-speaking.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰有波兰地主精英阶层，他们说波兰语。

sentences.en: There are millions of what were then called Ruthenian peasants.
sentences.zh: 有数百万当时被称为鲁塞尼亚人的农民。

sentences.en: So these are the people that will become Ukrainians.
sentences.zh: 也就是后来将成为乌克兰人的人群。

sentences.en: In the towns in particular, there is a Jewish population.
sentences.zh: 特别是在城镇里，居住着犹太人人口。

sentences.en: It's a great place for kind of Jewish settlements and Jewish culture.
sentences.zh: 这里是犹太人定居点和犹太文化的绝佳土壤。

sentences.en: And there are lots and lots of kind of runaways, fugitives, freebooters, outlaws and adventurers.
sentences.zh: 还有许许多多各种各样的逃亡者、逃犯、自由民、法外之徒和冒险家。

sentences.en: The people of what you might call the Wild EaSt.
sentences.zh: 也就是你可能会称之为“荒蛮东部”的人们。

sentences.en: And these were originally called Kazakhs or indeed Cossacks.
sentences.zh: 这些人最初被称为卡扎克，也就是现在的哥萨克。

sentences.en: These people have carved out their own kind of slightly semi-nomadic existence on the steppes.
sentences.zh: 这些人在这片乌克兰草原上开创了他们自己那种半游牧式的生活方式。

sentences.en: Of Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰的。

sentences.en: Because these are the old stamping grounds of the Scythians, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为这里是古代斯基泰人的活动范围，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So it's very suited to horse-born raiders and all that.
sentences.zh: 所以这里非常适合骑马劫掠者之类的人。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Who have their own kind of traditions.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有自己的一套传统。

sentences.en: And they've sort of developed their real mix of kind of ruffians and ne'er-do-wells and exiles and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 他们逐渐融合了真正的暴徒、无赖、流亡者等等群体。

sentences.en: And over time, over the decades and the centuries, they've developed their own traditions.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，经历了数十年和数个世纪，他们发展出了自己的传统。

sentences.en: Their own distinctive identity as Cossacks.
sentences.zh: 他们作为哥萨克人独特的身份认同。

sentences.en: They love a furry hat.
sentences.zh: 他们非常喜欢毛皮帽子。

sentences.en: And his rebellion against his Polish overlords.

sentences.en: The Cossacks had revolted.
sentences.zh: 哥萨克人起义了。

sentences.en: And they'd revolted against the Poles.

sentences.zh: 这是俄罗斯沙皇的附庸国。

sentences.en: And this is where Charles is now heading, towards the Zaporozhian hetmonate.
sentences.zh: 这也是查理现在正前往的地方，也就是扎波罗热酋长国。

sentences.en: And the reason he's doing this is because he's been driven out of Severia, the province of Russia, where he was last, because the Russian army is now advancing very quickly.

sentences.en: So actually, all these Latin speakers, I mean, him and Charles, they'll chat away in Latin.

sentences.zh: 并在他死后推选他的继承人。

sentences.en: He actually hates Menshikov already and he thinks, oh no, nightmare.
sentences.zh: 其实他已经开始痛恨缅什科夫了，心想，哦不，这真是个噩梦。

sentences.en: So, he summons his 2,000 closest and most loyal retainers and they mount their horses and they ride out of Baturin for the Swedish camp to rendezvous with Charles.
sentences.zh: 于是，他召集了2000名最亲信、最忠诚的随从，他们骑上马，离开巴图林前往瑞典军营，去和查理会合。

sentences.en: So, when Menshikov finally arrives at the Cossack citadel with a small force of dragoons, he finds that Mazepa is long gone.
sentences.zh: 因此，当缅什科夫率领一小支龙骑兵终于抵达这座哥萨克城堡时，他发现马泽帕早就逃之夭夭了。

sentences.en: And he immediately reports to Peter, disaster.
sentences.zh: 他立刻向彼得汇报：大难临头了。

sentences.en: Mazepa has deserted us and thrown in his lot with Charles the 12th.
sentences.zh: 马泽帕抛弃了我们，投靠了瑞典国王查理十二世。

sentences.en: But he's only taken 2,000.
sentences.zh: 但他只带走了2000人。

sentences.en: He hasn't taken the rest of the Cossacks.
sentences.zh: 他没有带走其余的哥萨克人。

sentences.en: He's only taken 2,000.
sentences.zh: 他只带走了2000人。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: He's then going to raise the rest of the Cossacks afterwards.
sentences.zh: 他打算随后再去召集剩下的哥萨克人。

sentences.en: So, Peter acts very quickly and very decisively.
sentences.zh: 所以，彼得的行动非常迅速、非常果断。

sentences.en: He orders Menshikov and his dragoons to fan out across the countryside to prevent anybody joining Mazepa.
sentences.zh: 他命令缅什科夫和他的龙骑兵在乡间散开，以防任何人去投奔马泽帕。

sentences.en: It does seem that Peter is getting the hang of war by this point.
sentences.zh: 看来到这个时候，彼得确实已经摸清了战争的门道。

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 的确如此。

sentences.en: Peter is really making a series of very good decisions now.
sentences.zh: 彼得现在确实做出了一系列非常正确的决定。

sentences.en: Like, very smart decisions.
sentences.zh: 比如，非常明智的决定。

sentences.en: You could argue it's easy to do that when circumstances are in your favour.
sentences.zh: 你可能会说，当形势对你有利时，这很容易做到。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But the Swedes are still a formidable adversary.
sentences.zh: 但瑞典人依然是一个强大的对手。

sentences.en: I mean, he's a guy who learns, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是一个懂得学习的人，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: Well, we saw going around shipyards in Amsterdam and London.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们看到他参观了阿姆斯特丹和伦敦的造船厂。

sentences.en: I mean, he's a man who enjoys learning things.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是一个喜欢学习新知识的人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he's making good, decisive, very ruthless, but effective decisions.
sentences.zh: 而且他正在做出正确、果断、非常冷酷但极其有效的决定。

sentences.en: So, he issues a public proclamation to the people of Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 于是，他向乌克兰人民发布了一份公开文告。

sentences.en: And he says, Mazepa is the new Judas.
sentences.zh: 他说，马泽帕就是新时代的犹大。

sentences.en: I mean, that's literally how he's described.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，文字上就是这么描述他的。

sentences.en: He has defected in order to put the land of Little Russia, as before, under the dominion of Poland and to turn the churches and monasteries over to the Catholic.
sentences.zh: 他背叛是为了像以前一样，把小俄罗斯的土地置于波兰的统治之下，并把教堂和修道院交给天主教徒。

sentences.en: Now, the interesting thing about this, of course, is there's no mention of the Swedes or Lutheranism, but it's playing on the deep dislike that the kind of ordinary sort of
sentences.zh: 当然，这里面有趣的地方在于，文告里完全没有提到瑞典人或路德宗，但它利用了普通

sentences.en: Ruthenian peasants and the Cossacks have for their former Polish overlords.
sentences.zh: 鲁塞尼亚农民和哥萨克人对他们昔日的波兰统治者根深蒂固的厌恶。

sentences.en: Yeah, very cunning.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常狡猾。

sentences.en: So, what's happening with Mazepa and Charles?
sentences.zh: 那么，马泽帕和查理那边情况如何？

sentences.en: Well, the Swedes have been delighted to see Mazepa.
sentences.zh: 嗯，瑞典人看到马泽帕非常高兴。

sentences.en: They've been very excited to see him.
sentences.zh: 他们看到他时都兴奋极了。

sentences.en: And, of course, Charles is delighted because he thinks, well, when we get to his citadel.
sentences.zh: 而且，查理当然也很高兴，因为他想，等我们到了他的城堡。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a Baturin.
sentences.zh: 对，就是巴图林。

sentences.en: Baturin must be full of all kinds of supplies and goodies, which is what they need.
sentences.zh: 巴图林一定囤满了各种物资和好东西，而这正是他们所需要的。

sentences.en: Supplies, gunpowder, fur hats.
sentences.zh: 物资、火药、皮帽。

sentences.en: Shelter.
sentences.zh: 栖身之所。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, by early November, they have crossed the rivers into the steps of central Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 所以，到了11月初，他们已经渡过河流，进入了乌克兰中部的草原。

sentences.en: And on the 11th of November, Charles's scouts glimpse Baturin on the horizon.
sentences.zh: 在11月11日，查理的侦察兵在地平线上隐约看到了巴图林。

sentences.en: So, fire, food, welcome.
sentences.zh: 太好了，有火、有食物、有欢迎。

sentences.en: But the closer they get, they see smoke rising overhead.
sentences.zh: 但他们越往前走，就看到滚滚浓烟升上天空。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.en: Because Baturin is burning.
sentences.zh: 因为巴图林正在燃烧。

sentences.en: While Charles had been on his way, Alexander Menshikov's dragoons had stormed the Cossack capital.
sentences.zh: 就在查理在赶来的路上时，亚历山大·缅什科夫的龙骑兵已经攻占了哥萨克首都。

sentences.en: They had slaughtered 6,000 men, women, and children.
sentences.zh: 他们屠杀了6000名男人、女人和儿童。

sentences.en: They had destroyed all the Cossack supplies and they had burned the fortress to the ground.
sentences.zh: 他们摧毁了所有的哥萨克物资，并将这座要塞烧成了灰烬。

sentences.en: And then they had held this public ceremony where they had officially stripped Mazepa of his title as the Hetman.
sentences.zh: 然后他们举行了一场公开仪式，正式剥夺了马泽帕的盖特曼称号。

sentences.en: They had dragged his portrait through the dust and then hanged it from the gallows beside the piles of butchered bodies.
sentences.zh: 他们把他的画像拖过尘土，然后挂在被屠杀的尸体堆旁边的绞刑架上。

sentences.en: And then they got the Metropolitan of Kiev, the sort of great churchman, to read a sentence of excommunication and anathema against Mazepa.
sentences.zh: 接着，他们找来基辅都主教这位伟大的教会人士，宣读了针对马泽帕的绝罚令与逐出教会的诅咒。

sentences.en: And amazingly, this was read out in Ukrainian churches every year until 1869, which is one reason, I guess,
sentences.zh: 令人惊奇的是，乌克兰的教堂每年都会宣读这一诅咒，一直持续到1869年，我想这也是为什么

sentences.en: why his name endures in Russia and Ukraine as this kind of great character of history.
sentences.zh: 他的名字在俄罗斯和乌克兰作为这样一个重要的历史人物流传至今的原因之一。

sentences.en: Of course, for the Russians, a great villain.
sentences.zh: 当然，对俄罗斯人来说，他是个大恶人。

sentences.en: And now for Ukrainian nationalists, they see him as much more of a hero.
sentences.zh: 而现在乌克兰民族主义者则认为他更像是一个英雄。

sentences.en: I mean, what is clear is that Charles XII and Peter the Great are two of history's great grudge holders.
sentences.zh: 显而易见的是，查理十二世和彼得大帝是历史上最记仇的两个人。

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, they are titanic in the grudges that they hold.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们记仇的程度简直是空前绝后。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But of course, this changes the picture for the war.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这改变了这场战争的格局。

sentences.en: First of all, it sends a very clear signal to all the other Cossacks.
sentences.zh: 首先，它向所有其他哥萨克人发出了一个非常清晰的信号。

sentences.en: If you join Mazepa and back Sweden, then Peter's wrath will be terrible, his retribution swift, to quote the Lord of the Rings.
sentences.zh: 如果你加入马泽帕并支持瑞典，那么正如《指环王》所说，彼得的怒火将无比可怕，他的报复将迅雷不及掩耳。

sentences.en: It means that Charles isn't going to get the food and supplies that he needs.
sentences.zh: 这意味着查理将无法获得他所需的食物和物资。

sentences.en: And it kind of makes Mazepa irrelevant now because he's just hanging around with Charles.
sentences.zh: 这也让马泽帕变得无足轻重了，因为他现在只能跟在查理身边混日子。

sentences.en: But what can he bring, Charles?
sentences.zh: 但他还能带来什么呢，查理？

sentences.en: He's no longer the leader of the Cossack.
sentences.zh: 他已经不再是哥萨克的领袖了。

sentences.en: But surely also, I mean, on the geopolitics of the war, it also means that it's mad that Charles XII is in Ukraine when he's a Swede who's aiming to march on Moscow.
sentences.zh: 但当然，从战争的地缘政治来看，这也意味着查理十二世作为一个旨在进军莫斯科的瑞典人，却跑到了乌克兰，这简直是疯了。

sentences.en: I mean, he's now essentially completely the wrong end of Europe.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他现在基本上完全跑到了欧洲的错误一端。

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: He's gone massively out of his way.
sentences.zh: 他已经偏离目的地十万八千里了。

sentences.en: And with nothing to show for it.
sentences.zh: 而且一无所获。

sentences.en: I mean, he's in as big a hole as he ever was.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他陷入了前所未有的大坑中。

sentences.en: A bigger one, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 也许是一个更大的坑。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because now the Russians are chasing him.
sentences.zh: 因为现在俄罗斯人正在追击他。

sentences.en: They're blocking the roads to the north.
sentences.zh: 他们封锁了通往北方的道路。

sentences.en: And as you say, he has no supplies.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他没有任何补给。

sentences.en: And now where are we?
sentences.zh: 那我们现在在哪里？

sentences.en: We're in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 我们在乌克兰。

sentences.en: In November, winter is coming.
sentences.zh: 在11月，冬天就要来了。

sentences.en: So now both sides hunker down for the winter.
sentences.zh: 所以现在双方都原地过冬。

sentences.en: If you look at a map of Ukraine, the Swedes are in a place called Hadiakh, which is roughly midway between Kiev and Kharkiv on today's map.
sentences.zh: 如果你看一眼乌克兰地图，瑞典人驻扎在一个叫加季亚奇的地方，在今天的地图上，它大约位于基辅和哈尔科夫的正中间。

sentences.en: The Russians are kind of blocking them in an arc to the northeast, stopping them from getting back up towards Moscow.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人在东北方向呈弧形将他们包围，阻止他们向莫斯科方向突围。

sentences.en: Although they're both on campaign in winter, this is a lot better for Peter.
sentences.zh: 尽管双方都在冬季行军，但这对外号称冬将军的彼得来说要好得多。

sentences.en: He's on home terrain.
sentences.zh: 他身处本土作战。

sentences.en: He's got loads of manpower and he's got time on his side.
sentences.zh: 他有大量的人力，而且时间站在他这一边。

sentences.en: And what's really crucial now is it's not just, as it were, the Russian or Ukrainian winter.
sentences.zh: 而现在真正关键的是，这不仅仅是通常意义上的俄国或乌克兰的冬天。

sentences.en: It's a winter like no other.
sentences.zh: 这是一个空前绝后的冬天。

sentences.en: Because we talked about this a long time ago, one of our early episodes about how the weather changed history.
sentences.zh: 因为我们很久以前就讨论过这一点，在我们的早期节目中谈到过天气是如何改变历史的。

sentences.en: This winter of 1708-1709 is the worst winter in Europe for 500 years.
sentences.zh: 1708年至1709年的这个冬天是欧洲500年来最寒冷的冬天。

sentences.en: The Baltic, the Seine, the Thames, the canals of Venice, even the Atlantic harbours, they all freeze over.
sentences.zh: 波罗的海、塞纳河、泰晤士河、威尼斯的运河，甚至连大西洋的港口，全都冻结了。

sentences.en: There are all these reports from all over Europe of farm animals freezing to death in the fields.
sentences.zh: 全欧洲都有这样的报道：农场动物在田野里被冻死。

sentences.en: In France alone, half a million people froze or starved to death.
sentences.zh: 仅在法国，就有五十万人被冻死或饿死。

sentences.en: And Dominic, even more importantly, doesn't the wine in Versailles freeze?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，更重要的是，凡尔赛宫里的葡萄酒是不是都冻住了？

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: The wine in Versailles froze.
sentences.zh: 凡尔赛宫的葡萄酒都冻结了。

sentences.en: The British economy shrunk by a quarter and didn't recover its value for years.
sentences.zh: 英国经济萎缩了四分之一，多年后才恢复元气。

sentences.en: And in the open steps of Ukraine, where there is no respite from the kind of howling snowstorms, it is just awful.
sentences.zh: 而在狂风呼啸的雪暴中毫无遮挡的乌克兰开阔草原上，情况简直糟透了。

sentences.en: And this is what we began with, that reading.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们一开始读的那段记载所描述的。

sentences.en: So this is where the bloke loses his foot to frostbite.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是那个家伙因为冻疮而失去脚的地方。

sentences.en: A Lutheran pastor who was with the Swedish army wrote afterwards,
sentences.zh: 一位随瑞典军队出征的路德宗牧师后来写道：

sentences.en: The spittle from people's mouths turned to ice before hitting the ground.
sentences.zh: 人们嘴里吐出的唾沫在落地之前就变成了冰。

sentences.en: Sparrows fell frozen from the roofs to the ground.
sentences.zh: 麻雀从屋顶上被冻僵掉落到地上。

sentences.en: You could see men without hands, others without hands and feet.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到失去双手的男人，还有失去双手双脚的人。

sentences.en: Some who had lost their fingers, faces, ears and noses.
sentences.zh: 有些人失去了手指、脸庞、耳朵和鼻子。

sentences.en: Others crawling around on all fours.
sentences.zh: 还有些人只能四肢着地爬行。

sentences.en: There were reports of kind of dragoons sitting on their horses,
sentences.zh: 有报道称，有些龙骑兵坐在马背上，

sentences.en: frozen solid with the reins in their hands.
sentences.zh: 手里抓着缰绳，已经彻底冻僵了。

sentences.en: And they have to be sort of sawn off to get them off the horse.
sentences.zh: 人们不得不把它们锯断才能把他们从马背上弄下来。

sentences.en: Oh God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So in all, perhaps 3,000 men, 3,000 Swedes froze to death.
sentences.zh: 总共有大约3000人，3000名瑞典士兵被活活冻死。

sentences.en: So how large is the force now?
sentences.zh: 那么现在这支军队还有多少人？

sentences.en: Probably well under 30,000, I would have said.
sentences.zh: 我敢说，大概远不到三万人。

sentences.en: That's a sizable number then.
sentences.zh: 那也算是一支不小的力量了。

sentences.en: Now the amazing thing is that Charles is still so reckless.
sentences.zh: 现在令人惊奇的是，查理依然如此鲁莽。

sentences.en: Not a scratch, but a trifle, as he said to that guy.
sentences.zh: 毫发无伤，不过是小事一桩，就像他对那家伙说的那样。

sentences.en: Yeah, not a trifle.
sentences.zh: 是的，可一点都不是小事。

sentences.en: So in January, he tries to attack, just to sort of liven things up a bit.
sentences.zh: 所以在1月份，他试图发动进攻，只是为了让局势稍微活跃一点。

sentences.en: He says, well, why don't we attack this Cossack village nearby?
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，我们为什么不进攻附近这个哥萨克村庄呢？

sentences.en: And he sends 3,000 men to attack this village.
sentences.zh: 于是他派了3000人去进攻这个村庄。

sentences.en: And he loses 400 of those men killed and 800 of them wounded.
sentences.zh: 结果他损失了400名阵亡士兵和800名负伤士兵。

sentences.en: Men he can ill afford to lose.
sentences.zh: 这些都是他损失不起的人手。

sentences.en: And one of the men who is wounded, and this will be important later, is his right-hand man, who we haven't mentioned yet.
sentences.zh: 其中一名受伤的人——这在日后非常重要——就是他的得力助手，我们之前还没提到过他。

sentences.en: And we'll talk about him in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我们将在下一期节目中详细讨论他。

sentences.en: Who is a guy called Field Marshal, Carl Gustav Reinskild.
sentences.zh: 他就是名叫陆军元帅卡尔·古斯塔夫·赖恩斯基尔德的家伙。
zh_words: 卡尔·古斯塔夫·赖恩斯基尔德

sentences.en: And he's hit by shrapnel in the chest and never really recovers.
sentences.zh: 他在胸部被榴弹碎片击中，自此之后就再也没有真正恢复健康。

sentences.en: So from this point onwards, Charles' right-hand man is kind of badly wounded.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个时候起，查理的得力助手就身受重伤了。

sentences.en: In the middle of February, Charles tries to get out of his kind of winter quarters and move east towards Kharkiv.
sentences.zh: 2月中旬，查理试图离开他的冬季营地，向东朝着哈尔科夫移动。

sentences.en: But yet more freak weather, thunderstorms, driving rain, floods.
sentences.zh: 但迎面而来的是更多反常的天气：雷暴、暴雨、洪水。

sentences.en: He has to go back.
sentences.zh: 他不得不折返。

sentences.en: And by the time he's ready to move again in April, his men are half-starved.
sentences.zh: 等到他在4月份准备再次出发时，他的手下已经处于半饥饿状态。

sentences.en: They're completely bedraggled.
sentences.zh: 他们狼狈不堪。

sentences.en: Their boots have rotted.
sentences.zh: 他们的靴子已经腐烂。

sentences.en: Their sodden uniforms are in rags.
sentences.zh: 他们湿漉漉的制服破烂不堪。

sentences.en: And their gunpowder is so wet that their artillery is basically useless.
sentences.zh: 他们的火药潮湿得厉害，以至于大炮基本上成了废铁。

sentences.en: And also a lot of their artillery, of course, is buried hundreds of miles to the north.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们的大部分大炮还埋在几百英里以北的地方。

sentences.en: What's his name that left them?
sentences.zh: 那个把它们留在那里的家伙叫什么名字？

sentences.en: Yeah, where Count Leuvenhaupt left them, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，就是勒文豪普特伯爵丢下它们的地方，没错。

sentences.en: Charles, of course, is still very jolly.
sentences.zh: 当然，查理依然兴致勃勃。

sentences.en: He sent a letter to our old friend Stanislav Leszczynski and said, my men are in very good condition and we're very close to winning the war.
sentences.zh: 他给我们的老朋友斯坦尼斯瓦夫·莱什琴斯基写了一封信，说我的部队状态极佳，我们离赢得战争已经咫尺之遥了。

sentences.en: And I think he genuinely believes it.
sentences.zh: 我想他是真心这么认为的。

sentences.en: You know, he's so convinced that they can't be beaten and that God is on their side.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他如此坚信他们是不可战胜的，上帝站在他们这一边。

sentences.en: It's a road bump.
sentences.zh: 只是一个小坎坷。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's a bump in the road.
sentences.zh: 这是路上的一个小波折。

sentences.en: But, you know, we can see the light at the end of the tunnel, if I'm not mixing my transport-based metaphors.
sentences.zh: 但你知道的，如果我的交通隐喻没有用混的话，我们能看到隧道尽头的曙光。

sentences.en: One of his chief advisors, in fact, his chief minister is a guy called Count Piper.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他的主要谋士之一，即他的首席大臣，是一个叫派珀伯爵的人。

sentences.en: I don't think it related to the Ensign Piper that we began with.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这和我们一开始提到的派珀少尉没关系。

sentences.en: He said to him, look, this is really the point where we should give up on this mad scheme.
sentences.zh: 他对他说，听着，这真的是我们该放弃这个疯狂计划的时候了。

sentences.en: Why don't we go west back to Poland?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么不往西回波兰呢？

sentences.en: And Charles said, no, no, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 查理却说，不，不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: What we actually need is to get reinforcements.
sentences.zh: 我们真正需要的是获得增援。

sentences.en: And he says, we'll send messengers to Sweden.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们会派信使去瑞典。

sentences.en: We will get the Polish Royal Army under Leszczynski to join us.
sentences.zh: 我们将让列什琴斯基率领的波兰皇家军队加入我们。

sentences.en: And I'm going to send envoys to the Crimean Tatars because they hate the Russians.
sentences.zh: 我还要派使节去克里米亚鞑靼人那里，因为他们痛恨俄罗斯人。

sentences.en: And once we've got all them on board, we can march north and take Moscow just as we thought.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们把他们都争取过来，我们就可以向北进军，就像我们想的那样攻占莫斯科。

sentences.en: And the mad thing is that Charles is so confident that when Peter sent a captured Swedish officer to suggest a compromise, to say, come on now, should we have peace?
sentences.zh: 最疯狂的是，查理是如此自信，以至于当彼得派出一名被俘的瑞典军官来建议妥协，说，算了吧，难道我们不该讲和吗？

sentences.en: Should we have a truce?
sentences.zh: 难道我们不该停战吗？

sentences.en: Because Charles did not even bother to reply because Peter was still saying, as part of the compromise, I'd like to keep us in Petersburg.
sentences.zh: 因为查理甚至懒得回复，因为彼得在作为妥协的一部分时，仍然说，我想让我们留在彼得堡。

sentences.en: So I said, oh, well, if you want to keep us in Petersburg, there's nothing to be talked about.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，好吧，如果你想让我们留在彼得堡，那就没什么好谈的了。

sentences.en: There's no way you're going to, you know, I'm going to win this war.
sentences.zh: 你绝对不可能，你知道的，我要赢得这场战争。

sentences.en: It's crazy.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Or heroic, depending on your perspective, or maybe both.
sentences.zh: 或者说很英勇，这取决于你的视角，或者两者兼有。

sentences.en: One battle can change the course of history.
sentences.zh: 一场战役就能改变历史的进程。

sentences.en: And Charles is a gambler.
sentences.zh: 而查理是个赌徒。

sentences.en: And gambles sometimes pay off.
sentences.zh: 赌博有时是有回报的。

sentences.en: We did the Battle of Hastings a few weeks ago, didn't we?
sentences.zh: 我们几周前才讲过黑斯廷斯战役，对吧？

sentences.en: And that did change the course of history.
sentences.zh: 那确实改变了历史进程。

sentences.en: And talking of battles, where is Charles heading now?
sentences.zh: 说到战役，查理现在正要去哪？

sentences.en: So in the end of April, Charles says to his men, we'll break camp.
sentences.zh: 所以在四月底，查理对他的手下说，我们要拔营。

sentences.en: We'll head southeast to a place where we can rendezvous with the Crimeans and with the Poles when they turn up.
sentences.zh: 我们要向东南进发，去一个可以与克里米亚人以及随后出现的波兰人会合的地方。

sentences.en: And the place he has in mind is a small town called Poltava on the bank of the River Vorskla.
sentences.zh: 他心目中的地方是沃尔斯克拉河畔一个叫波尔塔瓦的小镇。

sentences.en: It's a kind of wooden fortress.
sentences.zh: 那是一种木造的要塞。

sentences.en: And it has a Russian garrison, about 5,000 men with cannons.
sentences.zh: 里面有俄罗斯的驻军，大约五千人，配备了大炮。

sentences.en: So it's quite like the kind of forts that you get in the American West in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 所以这很像十九世纪你在美国西部能看到的那些堡垒。

sentences.en: Yeah, a little bit.
sentences.zh: 对，有点像。

sentences.en: That's exactly how I imagine it.
sentences.zh: 我就是这么想象的。

sentences.en: Because I imagine this landscape, having never been to Ukraine, I imagine it as being sort of quite American WeSt.
sentences.zh: 因为我从未去过乌克兰，所以我对这里的地貌想象，觉得它有点像美国西部。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Kind of Nobler's Creek.
sentences.zh: 有点像诺布勒克里克。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Nobler's Gulch.
sentences.zh: 诺布勒峡谷。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So by May 1709, Charles' army is entrenched west of this town.
sentences.zh: 所以在1709年5月，查理的军队在这个城镇以西挖好了战壕。

sentences.en: Now, this is very unusual for the Swedes because they don't normally like sieges, a bit like their Viking forebears, actually.
sentences.zh: 现在，这对于瑞典人来说非常罕见，因为他们通常不喜欢围城，其实这有点像他们的维京祖先。

sentences.en: And many of Charles' officers are a bit confused why they're laying siege to this actually reasonably insignificant fort.
sentences.zh: 查理的许多军官都有点困惑，为什么他们要围攻这个其实相当微不足道的堡垒。

sentences.en: And the reason they think is that actually the siege is a lure.
sentences.zh: 他们认为原因其实是这场围城是一个诱饵。

sentences.en: He's hoping to lure Peter the Great to battle because Charles is confident in a set piece pitched battle he will always win.
sentences.zh: 他希望能引诱彼得大帝出来决战，因为查理坚信在阵地战中他总是会赢。

sentences.en: This siege drags on for six weeks.
sentences.zh: 这场围城战拖了六周。

sentences.en: The weather is now, ironically, becoming punishingly hot.
sentences.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，现在天气变得酷热难耐。

sentences.en: You can't win.
sentences.zh: 你赢不了。

sentences.en: No, you can't.
sentences.zh: 不，你赢不了。

sentences.en: So the Swedes, in their rags with their salt and gunpowder, are sort of dripping with sweat, being beset by flies.
sentences.zh: 所以瑞典人们衣衫褴褛，带着盐和火药，浑身是汗，备受苍蝇骚扰。

sentences.en: Well, the Swedes don't like heat.
sentences.zh: 好吧，瑞典人不喜欢炎热。

sentences.en: They don't like heat.
sentences.zh: 他们不喜欢炎热。

sentences.en: Except in a sauna.
sentences.zh: 桑拿除外。

sentences.en: I love a Swedish summer.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢瑞典的夏天。

sentences.en: As you know, I've been on holidays, Sweden.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，我去过瑞典度假。

sentences.en: I know you do.
sentences.zh: 我知道你去了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I like a Baltic dip.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢在波罗的海泡个澡。

sentences.en: I think it's lovely and sunny.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那里又可爱又晴朗。

sentences.en: Swedish tourist boards should get in touch.
sentences.zh: 瑞典旅游局应该联系我们。

sentences.en: I think it's really nice and sunny.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那里真的很好很晴朗。

sentences.en: And I think it's not too hot.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得不会太热。

sentences.en: And I like that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢那样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Kind of one of those white beaches, but a black sky overhead.
sentences.zh: 有点像那种白色的沙滩，但头顶是黑色的天空。

sentences.en: It's very romantic.
sentences.zh: 非常浪漫。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That's Iceland.
sentences.zh: 那是冰岛。

sentences.en: A black beach with a black sky.
sentences.zh: 黑色的沙滩配黑色的天空。

sentences.en: We had it on Gotland.
sentences.zh: 我们在哥特兰岛见过。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 他们确实见过。

sentences.en: Gotland is absolutely gorgeous.
sentences.zh: 哥特兰岛绝对美极了。

sentences.en: I really recommend Gotland to people.
sentences.zh: 我真的很向大家推荐哥特兰岛。

sentences.en: We are approaching one of the great battles in world history.
sentences.zh: 我们正在接近世界历史上最伟大的战役之一。

sentences.en: And here we are talking about Swedish tourist spots.
sentences.zh: 而我们却在这里谈论瑞典的旅游景点。

sentences.en: Come on.
sentences.zh: 拜托。

sentences.en: Discipline.
sentences.zh: 有点纪律。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So the Swedes are outside Poltava.
sentences.zh: 所以瑞典人在波尔塔瓦城外。

sentences.en: So think of it this way.
sentences.zh: 你可以这样想。

sentences.en: The Swedes on the left-hand side of the picture, as you look at it, then the town, then a river.
sentences.zh: 瑞典人在你看到的画面的左侧，然后是城镇，然后是一条河。

sentences.en: And then on the right-hand side of the picture, on the eastern bank, the Russian army is assembling under Boris Sheremitev and Alexander Menshikov,
sentences.zh: 接着在画面的右侧，在东岸，俄罗斯军队在鲍里斯·舍列梅捷夫和亚历山大·缅什科夫的带领下集结，

sentences.en: who are then joined by Peter the Great.
sentences.zh: 随后彼得大帝也加入了他们。

sentences.en: So all the kind of Russian big guns.
sentences.zh: 所以全都是俄罗斯的大人物。

sentences.en: All the lads.
sentences.zh: 全都是小伙子们。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, all this time, Peter's strategy has been to avoid a big battle with the Swedes.
sentences.zh: 然而这段时间以来，彼得的战略一直是避免与瑞典人进行大决战。

sentences.en: But now he's beginning to rethink.
sentences.zh: 但现在他开始重新考虑了。

sentences.en: He has about 80,000 men.
sentences.zh: 他大约有八万兵力。

sentences.en: The Swedes have about 30,000, he thinks.
sentences.zh: 他认为瑞典人大约有三万。

sentences.en: And, you know, many of them with no toes.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，他们当中很多人都没有脚趾。

sentences.en: And they haven't got any gunpowder either.
sentences.zh: 他们也没有任何火药。

sentences.en: Gunpowder is all, yeah, absolutely dripping with water.
sentences.zh: 火药全都被水浸透了，对，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Peter's agents have told him that Poltava will probably fall by the end of June.
sentences.zh: 彼得的密探告诉他，波尔塔瓦可能会在六月底前陷落。

sentences.en: He really needs to strike before that because he doesn't want Charles to get into the fort and then to use it as a base.
sentences.zh: 他真的需要在那之前发动进攻，因为他不想让查理进入堡垒并以此为基地。

sentences.en: So Peter summons his commanders and he says, look, this is the moment.
sentences.zh: 于是彼得召集他的指挥官们说，听着，就是现在。

sentences.en: We'll get our army across the river to the western bank and then we'll unleash our artillery and our weight of numbers against the Swedes.
sentences.zh: 我们要把军队渡过河到达西岸，然后我们将对瑞典人释放我们的炮火和数量优势。

sentences.en: The difficulty is in crossing the River Vorskla.
sentences.zh: 困难在于渡过沃尔斯克拉河。

sentences.en: It's a wide, deep and marshy river.
sentences.zh: 那是一条宽阔、深邃且多沼泽的河流。

sentences.en: And he says, well, we'll cross further north, seven miles north of the town where it's a little bit shallower and we should be able to get across.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，我们往北走，在镇子以北七英里水浅一点的地方渡河，我们应该能过去。

sentences.en: The Swedes know that the Russians are going to do this.
sentences.zh: 瑞典人知道俄罗斯人会这么做。

sentences.en: Their scouts have reported on it.
sentences.zh: 他们的侦察兵已经汇报了这一点。

sentences.en: So by about the 15th and 16th of June, they are on full battle alert.
sentences.zh: 所以在6月15日和16日左右，他们处于全面战备状态。

sentences.en: Their plan is set.
sentences.zh: 他们的计划已经制定好了。

sentences.en: Field Marshal Rainskjord will take care of the Russians.
sentences.zh: 元帅伦舍尔将负责对付俄罗斯人。

sentences.en: He will let their vanguard across first and then he will fall on them and destroy them before the rest of the Russian force can join them.
sentences.zh: 他会先放他们的先头部队过去，然后在其余的俄军主力加入之前扑上去消灭他们。

sentences.en: It's a good plan.
sentences.zh: 这是个好计划。

sentences.en: And then the next day, Charles XII's birthday.
sentences.zh: 然后第二天，也就是查理十二世的生日。

sentences.en: Fate takes a hand.
sentences.zh: 命运插手了。

sentences.en: So Charles is turning 27.
sentences.zh: 所以查理迎来了27岁生日。

sentences.en: And so far in these 27 years, he has laughed in the face of danger and death.
sentences.zh: 在这27年里，他一直对危险和死亡报以嘲笑。

sentences.en: He's ridden the horses off cliffs.
sentences.zh: 他曾骑马冲下悬崖。

sentences.en: He's wrestled with bears.
sentences.zh: 他曾与熊搏斗。

sentences.en: Yeah, he has gone in full view of Russian gunners and he's had horses shot under him and God has always smiled on him.
sentences.zh: 是的，他曾大摇大摆地暴露在俄罗斯炮手的视野中，他的坐骑也曾被击中身亡，而上帝总是对他微笑。

sentences.en: But the story today on his birthday will be very different.
sentences.zh: 但今天在他生日这天，故事将截然不同。

sentences.en: At dawn, he rides out with his elite bodyguard who are called the Drabants to inspect the Swedish defences on the river.
sentences.zh: 黎明时分，他带着被称为近卫军的精锐保镖骑马出营，去检查河上的瑞典防线。

sentences.en: And Russian musketeers, just as usual, on the other side of the river, open fire and Charles completely ignores them.
sentences.zh: 河对岸的俄罗斯火枪手一如既往地开火了，而查理完全不理会他们。

sentences.en: And he's just turned away to ride his horse back up the bank when a Russian musket ball smacks into the left heel of his boot,
sentences.zh: 就在他刚转过身准备骑马返回岸上时，一颗俄罗斯火药枪弹击中了皮靴的左后跟，

sentences.en: travels right through his foot and it comes out through his big toe.
sentences.zh: 直接穿透了他的脚，并从他的大脚趾穿出。

sentences.en: Now, unbelievably, or indeed believably, if you've been following Charles's career till now, he doesn't flinch.
sentences.zh: 令人难以置信的是，或者如果你一直关注查理到目前为止的生平，其实也并不难置信，他连眼睛都没眨一下。

sentences.en: A Polish nobleman who's with him sees this, but Charles says, don't you dare say a word.
sentences.zh: 随行的一位波兰贵族看到了这一幕，但查理说，你敢说出一个字试试。

sentences.en: There goes your foot.
sentences.zh: 你的脚都没了。

sentences.en: Good Lord.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So it does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: That kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 就是那种事。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then he continues the tour of the defences without saying anything for another three hours.
sentences.zh: 然后他继续巡视防御工事，一声不吭地又坚持了三个小时。

sentences.en: I mean, that is insane, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太疯狂了，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, can you imagine?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你能想象吗？

sentences.en: I mean, if I had a blister, I'd be straight back to the camp and demanding medical attention.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果我脚上长了个水泡，我马上就会回营地要求医疗救助了。

sentences.en: He's a proper hero in that sense.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，他真是个英雄。

sentences.en: I mean, if a hero is a kind of someone who is midway between the mortal and the divine, I mean, that is superhuman.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果英雄是指介于凡人与神明之间的人，那简直就是超人。

sentences.en: This is such Alexander the Great behaviour.
sentences.zh: 这太像亚历山大大帝的行径了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Isn't it?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: It's absolutely Alexander the Great behaviour.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是亚历山大大帝的行径。

sentences.en: So he gets back to the camp riding his horse, of course, his foot in the stirrup.
sentences.zh: 于是他骑着马回到了营地，当然，脚还踩在马镫里。

sentences.en: He is deathly pale when he gets back there and blood is literally oozing out of his boot.
sentences.zh: 他回到营地时面色惨白，靴子里简直在往外渗血。

sentences.en: And as he tries to dismount, he puts his foot down.
sentences.zh: 当他试图下马时，他把脚踩在地上。

sentences.en: The pain is so overwhelmingly agonising.
sentences.zh: 那种痛苦是如此难以承受的剧烈。

sentences.en: He collapses in a dead faint.
sentences.zh: 他昏死过去。

sentences.en: And they rush around him.
sentences.zh: 人们立刻围了过去。

sentences.en: They see there's all this blood pouring out of his boot.
sentences.zh: 他们看到有血从靴子里不断涌出。

sentences.en: His foot has become so swollen, they have to cut his boot off.
sentences.zh: 他的脚肿得太厉害了，他们不得不把靴子割开。

sentences.en: And they find inside the bones of his foot have been shattered.
sentences.zh: 他们发现里面的脚骨已经被粉碎了。

sentences.en: And his foot is full of splinters of bone.
sentences.zh: 他的脚里满是碎骨头。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: You see, I feel like fainting just hearing that.
sentences.zh: 你看，我光是听到这事就觉得快要晕倒了。

sentences.en: The doctors hesitate when they see this.
sentences.zh: 医生们看到这一幕时犹豫了。

sentences.en: They're like, oh my God.
sentences.zh: 他们就像是，哦我的天哪。

sentences.en: And Charles, this is the best bit.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯，最精彩的部分来了。

sentences.en: He wakes up, he comes out, he looks at the doctors and says this brilliant line, slash away, slash away.
sentences.zh: 他醒来，走出来，看着医生们说了这句绝妙的话：切掉，切掉。

sentences.en: And then he picks up a pair of scissors and cuts into his foot himself to open it up for them.
sentences.zh: 然后他拿起一把剪刀，亲自动手在自己的脚上割开，好让他们能处理。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: So anyone who's prone to kind of, you know, moaning, bear that in mind.
sentences.zh: 所以任何容易发牢骚、你知道的、抱怨的人，把这点记在心里。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Think of the Swedish king and man up.
sentences.zh: 想想瑞典国王，拿出点男子气概来。

sentences.en: So the news spreads through the Swedish camp.
sentences.zh: 于是消息在瑞典军营里传开了。

sentences.en: The king has been hurt, all this.
sentences.zh: 国王受伤了，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Charles says initially before he passes out, I'll be back in the saddle before you know it.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯在昏迷前最初说道，一眨眼我就能重回马鞍上了。

sentences.en: In fact, his foot becomes very badly infected and he comes down with fever.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他的脚严重感染，并开始发烧。

sentences.en: Two days later, the 19th of June, the infection has spread up to his knee and the surgeons want to amputate his leg.
sentences.zh: 两天后的6月19日，感染已经蔓延到他的膝盖，外科医生们想要截肢。

sentences.en: And the only reason they don't is because they're terrified that when he wakes up, you know,
sentences.zh: 他们之所以没有这样做，唯一的理由是他们害怕等他醒来，你知道的，

sentences.en: he will have them attacked by a bear or something in punishment because the thought of losing his leg would be so dreadful for him.
sentences.zh: 他会作为惩罚让一头熊或其他什么东西来攻击他们，因为失去这条腿对他来说简直太可怕了。

sentences.en: So they don't do it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们没有动手。

sentences.en: By the 21st, two days after that, it is pretty clear to them that he will die within hours.
sentences.zh: 到了21日，也就是两天后，他们非常清楚他会在几个小时内死去。

sentences.en: And in fact, at this point, his childhood servant has been summoned to his bedside to read him his favourite boyhood fairy tales.
sentences.zh: 事实上，就在这时，他童年时的仆人被召到床边，给他读他最喜欢的童年童话。

sentences.en: That's nice.
sentences.zh: 那挺好的。

sentences.en: Isn't that touching?
sentences.zh: 不是很感人吗？

sentences.en: Now, meanwhile, Field Marshal Rainsgild has come back from the river, which he was meant to be defending, to be with the king.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，陆军元帅雷恩斯吉尔德从他本该防守的河边回来，陪伴国王。

sentences.en: And he says to the other officers, look, we can't fight this, you know, death or glory battle while the king is lying dying.
sentences.zh: 他对其他军官说，听着，当国王躺着等死时，我们没法进行这种生死之战。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: They're so shaken by the loss of their leader, but also we need to be with him and we need to be on hand when he does die.
sentences.zh: 他们因失去领袖而深受打击，但我们也需要陪着他，并且在他真的死去时随时待命。

sentences.en: That's madness.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Well.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: What would he want?
sentences.zh: 他会希望怎么样？

sentences.en: He would want them to go and fight.
sentences.zh: 他会希望他们去战斗。

sentences.en: I suppose he would, but they're very loyal, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 我想他是会这么希望，但他们非常忠诚，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, but if you're loyal, you obey your king's orders.
sentences.zh: 对，但如果你忠诚，你就会服从国王的命令。

sentences.en: Well.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I just feel Charles is, you know, he's being let down left, right and centre by all his, I suppose, I mean, he's appointed.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得查尔斯，你知道的，他被他所有的——我想我是指他任命的那些人——四面八方地背叛了。

sentences.en: So it's his fault to that extent.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说这也是他的错。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It's all Charles' fault ultimately, is it?
sentences.zh: 归根结底全都是查尔斯的错，是吗？

sentences.en: That's Paul from Utah.
sentences.zh: 那是来自犹他州的保罗。

sentences.en: Well, he's in command.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他是总指挥。

sentences.en: You're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 你完全说得对。

sentences.en: Because while he's lying there on his deathbed, the Russians do cross to the Western Bank.
sentences.zh: 因为正当他躺在病榻上时，俄国人确实渡到了西岸。

sentences.en: Of course, they're still a long way.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们离得很远。

sentences.en: They're seven miles north of Poltava, but they're now on the same side of the bank as the Swedes.
sentences.zh: 他们在波尔塔瓦以北七英里处，但他们现在和瑞典人在同一侧岸上了。

sentences.en: And they've lost the chance to inflict, you know, a murderous descent on them.
sentences.zh: 而瑞典人已经失去了对他们发动，你知道的，致命突袭的机会。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And the Russians have pulled off the most difficult bit of Peter's plan without really facing an enemy shot.
sentences.zh: 而且俄国人在几乎没有遭到敌方射击的情况下，完成了彼得计划中最困难的部分。

sentences.en: Oh, it makes me weep for the Swedes.
sentences.zh: 哦，这让我为瑞典人感到痛心。

sentences.en: Then on the 22nd of June, two dramatic developments.
sentences.zh: 接着在6月22日，发生了两个戏剧性的进展。

sentences.en: First of all, there's sort of movement in Charles' tent and then to the light of his troops.
sentences.zh: 首先，查尔斯的帐篷里似乎有动静，随后在士兵们兴奋的目光中，

sentences.en: He is brought out on a stretcher.
sentences.zh: 他被用担架抬了出来。

sentences.en: He is not dead.
sentences.zh: 他没有死。

sentences.en: The fever has broken against all the odds.
sentences.zh: 克服了所有的艰难险阻，他的高烧终于退了。

sentences.en: He is still very weak, but he is alive and he is kind of saluting to them.
sentences.zh: 他仍然非常虚弱，但他还活着，而且还在向他们敬礼。

sentences.en: And then as he's lying there on the stretcher, the messengers arrive from the Poles and the Crimean Tatars.
sentences.zh: 然后正当他躺在担架上时，波兰人和克里米亚鞑靼人的信使到了。

sentences.en: And guess what?
sentences.zh: 你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: The Crimeans aren't coming.
sentences.zh: 克里米亚人不来了。

sentences.en: Their Ottoman overlords have said, no, don't help the Swedes.
sentences.zh: 他们的奥斯曼宗主说，不，不要去帮瑞典人。

sentences.en: And what is worse, the Poles aren't coming either.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，波兰人也不来了。

sentences.en: This bloke, Stanislaw Fleschinski, Charles' puppet, has completely let him down.
sentences.zh: 这家伙，斯坦尼斯瓦夫·莱什钦斯基，查尔斯的傀儡，彻底让他失望了。

sentences.en: He says, oh, my kingdom is too insecure.
sentences.zh: 他说，哦，我的王国太不稳定了。

sentences.en: My rule is a little bit fragile.
sentences.zh: 我的统治有点脆弱。

sentences.en: It'd be reckless for me to send an army to help you now.
sentences.zh: 现在派军队去帮你们太轻率了。

sentences.en: I mean, he may have a great name, but that's poor behavior.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他可能名气很大，但这种行为真糟糕。

sentences.en: It is poor behavior.
sentences.zh: 这确实行为糟糕。

sentences.en: So Count Piper at this point, the minister, he says to Charles, we must get out of here immediately.
sentences.zh: 所以大臣派普伯爵在这个时候对查尔斯说，我们必须马上离开这里。

sentences.en: This is a disaster.
sentences.zh: 这是一场灾难。

sentences.en: We must head for the rivers of Dnieper, cross it, get into Poland, sign a truce with Peter if we have to.
sentences.zh: 我们必须前往第聂伯河，渡过河，进入波兰，如果有必要的话就和彼得签定休战协议。

sentences.en: We just have to escape with you and the army intact.
sentences.zh: 我们必须带着你和完整的军队逃跑。

sentences.en: And Charles says to him, under no circumstances, there'll be no retreat.
sentences.zh: 而查尔斯对他说，绝无可能，绝对不撤退。

sentences.en: There's no deal with Peter the Great.
sentences.zh: 绝不与彼得大帝做交易。

sentences.en: Now, the thing is, Charles' mental state at this point must be very, I mean, that must be very fragile.
sentences.zh: 现在的问题是，查尔斯此时的精神状态一定非常，我是说，那一定非常脆弱。

sentences.en: Because he's nearly died.
sentences.zh: 因为他差点死了。

sentences.en: He's only just coming out of a fever.
sentences.zh: 他才刚退烧。

sentences.en: Basically, the inside of his foot has been shredded, hasn't eaten a square meal for about 12 months.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他脚的内部已经被撕裂了，而且已经有大约12个月没吃过一顿正餐了。

sentences.en: I wonder if, I mean, he's almost died, but he hasn't.
sentences.zh: 我在想，我的意思是，他差点死了，但他没有死。

sentences.en: Has God preserved him?
sentences.zh: 是上帝保佑了他吗？

sentences.en: I think there's a big element of that.
sentences.zh: 我认为这里面很大一部分原因是这样。

sentences.en: I think he's sitting there probably with a kind of sheen of cold sweat on his face, thinking, I've cheated death once again.
sentences.zh: 我想他当时可能坐在那里，脸上一层冷汗，心想，我又一次战胜了死神。

sentences.en: Fate has spared me for higher things.
sentences.zh: 命运留着我去做更高更大的事。

sentences.en: And I think he also thinks, enough of this now.
sentences.zh: 我想他同时也在想，这些够了。

sentences.en: Well, you know, Peter is only seven miles away.
sentences.zh: 你看，彼得只有七英里远。

sentences.en: Let's finish this.
sentences.zh: 让我们了结此事吧。

sentences.en: Let's have the pitch battle that I've always wanted.
sentences.zh: 让我们进行我一直渴望的正面决战。

sentences.en: I don't think he ever doubts that he will win it.
sentences.zh: 我认为他从未怀疑过自己会赢。

sentences.en: Because on the Sunday, the 27th of June, five days later, they have their morning prayers.
sentences.zh: 因为在星期天，6月27日，五天后，他们做了早祷。

sentences.en: And then he calls his generals to his bedside.
sentences.zh: 然后他把将军们召集到床边。

sentences.en: And he says, the Russians may have the greater numbers, but we have the experience.
sentences.zh: 他说，俄国人可能人数更多，但我们有经验。

sentences.en: We have the tactics and we have God's support.
sentences.zh: 我们有战术，我们有上帝的支持。

sentences.en: If we take them unawares, if we strike first, we can trap them against the river.
sentences.zh: 如果我们出其不意，如果我们率先出击，我们就能把他们困在河边。

sentences.en: We can smash their army and we could maybe even capture Peter himself.
sentences.zh: 我们可以粉碎他们的军队，甚至可能抓住彼得本人。

sentences.en: And if we do that, then we win the war, you know, in a morning.
sentences.zh: 如果我们做到了这一点，那么我们就在一个早晨赢得了这场战争。

sentences.en: And he says, tomorrow, outside Poltava, we will have the final showdown to decide the fate of Northern and Eastern Europe.
sentences.zh: 他说，明天，在波尔塔瓦郊外，我们将进行决定北方和东欧命运的最终决战。

sentences.en: Tom, the winner takes it all.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，胜者拥有一切。

sentences.en: The loser has to fall.
sentences.zh: 败者黯然退场。

sentences.en: We'll be standing small.
sentences.zh: 我们将显得渺小。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so it is that in the early hours of the following morning, the final showdown, the battle of Poltava begins.
sentences.zh: 就这样，在第二天清晨，最终的决战，波尔塔瓦战役开始了。

sentences.en: Well, who will win it?
sentences.zh: 那么，谁会赢呢？

sentences.en: There's only one way to find out.
sentences.zh: 只有一个方法能找到答案。

sentences.zh: 那就是如果你是“历史其余部分”俱乐部的会员，就可以直接去收听我们对这场史诗般战役的讲述。

sentences.zh: 如果你不是，你仍然可以前往 therestishistory.com 并注册来收听。

sentences.zh: 或者你可以等到下周。

sentences.en: Yeah, don't wait.
sentences.zh: 是的，别等了。

sentences.zh: 但无论你选择什么，我们下期将回归进行最终的决战。

sentences.zh: 再见。
